broader_venue_comparison.roles: 12 recent TOPLAS, 5 high-visibility same-venue substitutes, and 6 adjacent-top-venue papers

novelty_delta: Current systems propose carriers, training objectives, data poisoning, error correction, or attack-specific impossibility. TOPLAS-19 instead derives exact feasibility and impossibility from declared behavioral, observational, attack, and source-access contracts, with realization, directed-compilation, list-recovery, product, compactness, and predicate boundaries.

subsumption_check.assessment: No subsumption established by the cited comparisons; not an exhaustive novelty or priority proof.
subsumption_check.review_basis: Prior corpus plus targeted publisher/author records and two corrected mechanism descriptions.

impact_calibration: The likely impact is diagnostic: certificates identify whether behavior, observation, robustness, or reachability blocks a channel before implementation. No claim of guaranteed adoption, acceptance, or award is made.

records.closest_overlap: Behavior-preserving syntactic carriers, detector labels, attack robustness, and payload capacity.
records.contribution_form: Concrete post-hoc multi-channel code watermark with error correction and enumerated attack evaluation.
records.delta_from_this_project: Assumes a fixed Python carrier inventory, keying scheme, and attack taxonomy; it does not classify arbitrary behavior/observation/access contracts or characterize when every source admits a globally consistent label family.
records.effect_on_claims: Narrows practical-impact prose; supports the need to separate a semantic capacity certificate from carrier engineering. Does not subsume the main theorems.
records.title: Multi-Channel Spread-Spectrum Code Watermarking
records.evidence_provenance: Archived scholarly-record metadata and recorded PDF hash; citation status is stated explicitly.

records.closest_overlap: Style-preserving transformations, black-box verification, removal attacks, and source/binary task variation.
records.contribution_form: Concrete dataset watermark and poison design evaluated across source and decompilation tasks.
records.delta_from_this_project: Protects a training dataset through model behavior; it does not define per-program source-dependent reachability or an exact quotient/incidence feasibility boundary.
records.effect_on_claims: Adds a current dataset-model comparison and prevents overgeneralizing the theory to training-data ownership. Does not subsume the main theorems.
records.title: DuCodeMark: Dual-Purpose Code Dataset Watermarking via Style-Aware Watermark–Poison Design
records.evidence_provenance: Archived scholarly-record metadata and recorded PDF hash; citation status is stated explicitly.

records.closest_overlap: Functional preservation, detectability, adversarial transformations, and source-conditioned generation.
records.contribution_form: Learned generation-time watermarking using reinforcement learning, compiler feedback, and a confidential verifier.
records.delta_from_this_project: Its guarantees and evidence depend on a trained generator/verifier and empirical distribution; it does not provide a mechanism-independent exact existence or impossibility classification.
records.effect_on_claims: Clarifies that the paper does not compare detection accuracy or learned-model performance. Does not subsume the semantic boundary.
records.title: SWaRL: Safeguard Code Watermarking via Reinforcement Learning
records.evidence_provenance: Archived scholarly-record metadata and recorded PDF hash; citation status is stated explicitly.

records.closest_overlap: Negative robustness boundaries under behavior-preserving transformations.
records.contribution_form: Attack-specific impossibility theorem and empirical obfuscation study for n-gram watermark detectors.
records.delta_from_this_project: Uses an n-gram detector family and distribution-consistency assumption; the present paper classifies arbitrary fixed detector/attack/access relations, exact messages, lists, products, and predicates.
records.effect_on_claims: Adds the closest current negative result and forces attack-specific wording. Complementary rather than subsuming.
